source:
A woman's cries of terror split the air from where she lay pinioned beneath the man, his drug-induced insanity painted across his face. Jon grabbed his shirt from behind and heaved with all of his strength. The man, completely unmoved, looked up at him from the ground, his expression turning from one of anger to bewilderment. Failing in his first effort, Jon slugged him across the face. The lack of force was more than made up for by the weight of Jon's gauntlet-ed fist and the man crumpled. 
 
 Jon reached out his hand to help the woman up but she scrambled away looking even more scared than she had a second ago. He tried to smile reassuringly and approached her. `` Do n't worry. I'm here to-'' Faster than he could react, the woman snatched a rock off the street and threw it clipping him in the forehead. 
 
 `` Oh shit!'' Jon stumbled back clutching his head and saw the women darting into an alley as his vision cleared. He looked at his hand and saw a smattering of blood. 
 
 `` You okay Jon?'' a voice called out from the down the street. He looked up and saw Matt approaching, his makeshift chair leg clubs in his hands. 
 
 `` Yea,'' he called back. `` Just a scratch.'' Jon had never considered himself imposing with his scrawny form and patchy beard that his mother was always telling him to trim. Seeing Matt come out of the smoke though, warpaint covering his bare chest and face, Jon realized how he might have given the woman the wrong impression. 
 
 Matt took a look at the cut in his forehead. `` Just a scratch!'' he said slapping him on the back. `` Probably wo n't even scar. Too bad really.'' 
 
 `` Is it safe?'' A quiet voice whimpered from an abandoned van behind them. 
 
 `` Yea Gary. All good,'' called back Matt and Gary, tripping over his long black robes, tumbled out of the van. He clutched a hardcover book to his chest like a shield and his enormous glasses had been knocked askew. 
 
 `` Anyone seen Jeff?'' Gary said. 
 
 In response came a bloodcurdling war cry through the smoke and a figure came flying at them. His fur cloak billowed out behind him and the bones curling up from his helmet lent the appearance of a demon out of Hell. The light of distant fires accentuated his rippling muscles and a criss-cross of tiny cuts covered his torso. In his hands was a largest ax Jon had ever seen. 
 
 The man came to a stop in front of them, a massive grin across his face. `` Jeff,'' said Jon, breaking the stunned silence. `` Where the hell did you find that ax?'' 
 
 Jeff barked a deep laugh towards the sky. `` Do not ask questions you do not wish to know the answers to little man. Do not fear. No Odin-fearing citizens were hurt in my conquest.'' 
 
 When Jon had moved to city for school with Matt and Gary and met Jeff they had n't been sure about playing D & D with him. Gary was the Dungeon Master though and he decided to give it a try and they found that playing with Jeff made the whole thing more real. He guessed that while he had always enjoyed playing his character, Jeff was his character. He'd been the one to get them into LARPing and helped them collect some of their own gear. 
 
 Of course, then the power had gone out and the world had gone to hell. Things had been alright at first, but as supplies and information had become scarce, chaos had swept in. Houses and stores were broken into and bodies started piling up in the streets. Jon and his friends had been left mercifully safe in their stocked third-story apartment, but as screams echoed in the air outside their window every night, they realized someone needed to do something. It had actually been Gary who realized it had to be them, and he knew exactly how they should do it. 
 
 So, donning their armor and adorning themselves in warpaint, they had gone out into the night, protecting people's homes and rescuing those unfortunate enough to be left helpless on the streets. Jon had been scared shitless at first, but with each person they saved, he'd found himself falling more and more into his character. It made him realize why he'd ever played in the first place. 
 
 `` By Odin's Raven!'' exclaimed Jeff interrupting his reverie. `` You've sustained an injury.'' He prodded the swelling bump on Jon's forehead bringing a fresh wave of pain. 
 
 `` Yea, yea. It's nothing,'' said Jon, shoving Jeff's hand away. `` Just a misunderstanding with some lady I rescued.'' 
 
 `` Ha!'' cried Jeff. `` If the damsels allowed themselves to be rescued easily, they would not be worth rescuing. Come friends! Evil abounds to the north at the crossroads of Maple and 7th!'' And off he went into the night, leaving the other three in his wake. 
 
 When they finally caught him, he was peaking over the hood of an overturned Jeep. He turned and moved his pointer finger over his lips signaling caution. They crept up next to him and peered over the hood to where he was looking. The headlights of two cars lit a scene out of a movie. Kneeling on the ground, their hands on their heads was a group of about twenty bedraggled-looking people. Around them stood six men, rifles in hand. Their leader was screaming at one of the women as helpless tears streamed down her face. 
 
 `` We have to help them,'' said Matt. `` They have children with them.'' Jon peaked out again and realized he was right. A boy and a girl that could n't be more than seven huddled against who must have been their father crying. 
 
 Despair sank in on Jon. He wanted to help as much as any of them, but who were they kidding? They had clubs and an ax. Those men out there had guns. All they would likely do was get those people killed. `` Listen Matt,'' he said. `` We all want to help but...'' 
 
 `` No,'' interrupted Gary. `` We have to help them.'' He was definitely terrified but a look of resolute steadfastness covered his face behind his glasses. 
 
 `` It is settled then,'' said Jeff, loudly enough to make them wince. `` The grace of Bestla will protect us.'' He hefted his ax. 
 
 Gary grabbed his arm. `` No, wait. We'll wo n't be any help without a plan, but I've got an idea.'' He opened up his book and unfolded a sheet of grid paper, pebbles and rubble quickly forming a rough map of the area around them. 
 
 As he finished laying out his strategy, a shout went up from the crowd. They peaked over just in time to see a man tear away from the kneeling group and try to run down the street. Shots rang out in the night behind him and he toppled down onto the ground bleeding. 
 
 `` It's now or never,'' said Gary. `` Go!'' 
 
 They spread out using the abandoned cars around them as cover. Any noise they might have made was covered by the shouting of the man and the echoing of sirens helplessly far away. Jon crept into a building on the opposite side of the intersection. The second floor had been gutted by fire and was left open to the elements. He found he had to balance his way across uncovered beams to get to his vantage point but that just made his job that much easier. 
 
 He gave the others a minute more to get into position but did n't dare wait any longer in case the men opened fire. He crouched behind the window pane, steeled himself and yelled. The man's tirade outside quieted. A second later he heard him bark a command and the sound of footsteps was followed by two men as they entered the building. 
 
 He tipped the remnants of an armoire from its precarious perch and it crashed onto the head of one of the men below toppling him. He dropped down after it catching his friend off guard. His misjudged the swing of his club though and brought it down on the man's shoulder definitely breaking something but not bringing the man down. 
 
 The man's cry of pain was choked out by gunshots as bullets ripped into the building around him. He was protected from the first volley by the man standing in front of him but he was forced into cover as the man fell. 
 
 The shots were replaced by cries of alarm and Jon stole a glance out the window. Silhouetted by the headlights of a car was a tornado of destruction. Jeff's ax felled one of the men before they'd known he was there. He closed the gap with a second before he could lift his rifle and they tumbled to the ground wrestling for control of the man's sidearm. The last grunt raised his rifle but was cut off by Matt who leaped out knocking the weapon from his hand. 
 
 The leader raised his weapon to aim at Matt but a pitifully squeaky battle-cry brought his attention around to Gary as he charged out from cover, his robes tied comically above his knees. He collided with the man but was thrown off tumbled to the ground. Jon scrambled up and charged out into the fray but there was no way he could make it in time. The man raised his gun and aimed. 
 
 His shot was knocked wide as the woman plowed into him from the side. The other captives were jolted out of their shock and swarmed to help piling on top of the man. Some split off to help Jeff and Matt and the fighting was quickly finished. 
 
 Jon shoved through the exultant crowd and knelt over Gary. He was n't moving. Jon grabbed him by the shoulders and shook him. `` Gary!'' 
 
 `` Ouch. Dammit! Jon, stop! That hurts!'' 
 
 Jon let go and Gary sat up. Blood trickled down his arm where the bullet had gone straight through. The shadows of Matt and Jeff loomed over them and Gary smiled. `` You remember what I said three months ago when we started the campaign? Well, I admit it. I was wrong.'' 
 
 Jon looked at his friends confused. `` I have no memory of this,'' bellowed Jeff behind him. 
 
 Matt spoke, a smile on his face. `` I think it was something like,'Three Barbarians? That will never work.'''

Perspective: The Woman (unnamed)

In the heart of chaos and despair, I found myself a pawn in this game of life, my identity lost amidst the crumbling remnants of society. The city was a labyrinth of danger, where every corner held a potential threat. That fateful night, as I walked along the deserted street, I never imagined that it would lead me to a world far beyond the confines of my own.

I felt a sudden, jarring collision, sending me tumbling into the shadows of an alleyway. The man who had accosted me was swiftly apprehended by a stranger, a man named Jon. He was tall and broad-shouldered, his eyes filled with determination as he pinned my attacker to the ground. Yet, there was a flicker of something more in those eyes—a spark of vulnerability that spoke of battles fought and won.

A moment later, I felt another blow that left me reeling. It was Jon, struck by the very person he sought to protect. Matt arrived soon after, his face a mask of concern as he helped Jon to his feet. I could see the tension between them, a bond forged in shared battles and mutual respect.

Gary appeared, hiding within an abandoned van, his eyes wide with fear and uncertainty. The streets were no place for the faint-hearted, and Gary was clearly tested by the night's events. Yet, there was a fire within him that could not be extinguished, a will to survive and protect others that would guide them through their perilous journey.

As we navigated the chaotic streets and confronted armed men who held innocents captive, I began to understand the true nature of these strangers. They were more than just players in a game; they were warriors, fighting for justice and protecting those who could not defend themselves.

The final battle was a blur of gunfire and adrenaline, a testament to their courage and resourcefulness. Despite being outnumbered and outgunned, they fought with tenacity and cunning, using their knowledge and experience to outmaneuver their enemies. Gary was wounded in the fray, but his spirit remained unbroken as he stood shoulder-to-shoulder with his friends.

The night ended with Gary's admission of his initial skepticism and Jeff's strange amnesia regarding the events that transpired. I watched them retreat to their safe haven, a third-story apartment in the heart of the city. I couldn't help but feel a sense of gratitude for their intervention, and a lingering curiosity about the bond that held them together.

In the end, they were not just heroes in a game—they were beacons of hope in a world plunged into darkness, a testament to the indomitable human spirit that refused to yield to despair. And as I disappeared back into the shadows of the city, I knew that somewhere out there, Jon, Matt, Gary, and Jeff would continue their mission, fighting for justice in a world gone mad.
